title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Monetary Determination and Redetermination Standard
content:
The monetary determination on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is computed from the base-period wages on record in the program's wage verification source.

## Base period

The standard base period is the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before the claim effective date. When the standard base period fails and the program allows it, the alternate base period of the last four completed calendar quarters is tested, and the base period actually used is recorded on the claim as standard or alternate.

## Eligibility and weekly amount (Regular State Unemployment Insurance, UCFE, UCX and Combined Wage Claim records)

1. The claim is monetarily eligible when high-quarter wages are at least the program's minimum high-quarter wages and base-period wages are at least the minimum ratio times high-quarter wages.
2. The weekly benefit amount is high-quarter wages divided by the divisor, rounded down to the whole dollar, then raised to the floor or lowered to the ceiling.
3. Retired clause, no longer in force: "The dependency allowance is the per-dependent amount times the number of dependents on record, counting no more than the maximum number of dependents." This clause is superseded by the current basis.
4. Retired clause, no longer in force: "The maximum benefit amount is the lesser of the maximum duration weeks times the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance and the base-period-wage fraction times base-period wages, rounded down to the whole dollar." This clause is superseded by the current basis.
5. Extended, trade and disaster programs are computed under the Department's entitlement rules for the Extended Benefits (EB), Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) and Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) programs.

## Effect of a determination

- An eligible determination sets the monetary status to eligible and credits the maximum benefit amount to the remaining benefit balance, and the first eligible determination activates a filed claim.
- An ineligible first determination sets the monetary status to ineligible, credits nothing and moves the filed claim to ineligible.
- Retired clause, no longer in force: "A monetary redetermination carries the next determination number and books only the difference from the previous maximum benefit amount: an increase is credited and a decrease is debited, and payments already issued are not reversed by the redetermination." This clause is superseded by the current basis.

## Redetermination on missing-wage proof

A redetermination request supported by missing-wage proof is accepted only when it is received no later than the redetermination request window after the monetary determination date. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the monetary determination date, and a request received on the last day of the window is timely. A later request is not a redetermination request and can only be pursued as an appeal of the monetary determination.

The monetary determination date read is the one on the claim records, not a date the claimant recalls.

| Day the request is received (calendar days after the monetary determination date) | Under a 21-day window |
|---|---|
| Day 1 through day 21 | Timely: accepted as a redetermination request |
| Day 22 or later | Not a redetermination request; pursued only as an appeal of the monetary determination |

### Hypothetical worked figures

- Weekly amount: high-quarter wages of 9000.00 divided by a divisor of 26 is 346.15, rounded down to 346; with a floor of 75.00 and a ceiling of 572.00 the weekly benefit amount is 346. High-quarter wages of 1950.00 give 75, already at the floor of 75.00.
- Eligibility: high-quarter wages of 4000.00 with base-period wages of 5800.00 fail a ratio of 1.5, because 1.5 times 4000.00 is 6000.00.
- Window: for a monetary determination dated on a Monday, a 21-day window ends on the Monday three weeks later; a request received that Monday is timely and one received the next day is not.

superseded_clauses: The maximum benefit amount is the lesser of the maximum duration weeks times the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance and the base-period-wage fraction times base-period wages, rounded down to the whole dollar.
The dependency allowance is the per-dependent amount times the number of dependents on record, counting no more than the maximum number of dependents.

A monetary redetermination carries the next determination_number and books only the difference from the previous maximum benefit amount: an increase is credited and a decrease is debited, and payments already issued are not reversed by the redetermination.
